content: The following individuals and organizations have contributed significantly to the global efforts in health and hygiene, particularly in the context of water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) in healthcare facilities: 1. Ministry of Health, Serbia: Represented by i.c., contributing to health initiatives in Serbia. 2. Waltaji Kutane: Affiliated with the World Health Organization (WHO) in Ethiopia, focusing on public health improvements. 3. Akosua Kwakye: A representative of WHO in Ghana, working on health-related programs. 4. Oyuntogos Lkhasuren: Associated with WHO in Lao PDR, addressing health and sanitation challenges. 5. Steve Luby: A scholar from Stanford University, USA, contributing to global health research. 6. Rolf Luyendijk: Representing the Water Supply and Sanitation Collaborative Council (WSSCC) in Switzerland, focusing on sanitation and hygiene. 7. Boniface Magtibay: A WHO representative in the Philippines, working on health and hygiene initiatives. 8. Shamsul Mahmud: Affiliated with WHO in Bangladesh, addressing public health concerns. 9. Guy Mbayu: A WHO representative in Congo, contributing to health programs. 10. Frances McConville: Based in Switzerland, working with WHO on global health strategies. 11. Francesco Mitis: Another WHO representative in Switzerland, focusing on health and sanitation. 12. Ian Moise: From Catholic Relief Services in the USA, contributing to health and humanitarian efforts. 13. Klaus Moldeus: Representing UN Water in Switzerland, focusing on water and sanitation. 14. Carolyn Moore: From the Global Handwashing Partnership in the USA, promoting hygiene practices. 15. Josephine Okine: A nurse from Ghana, contributing to healthcare delivery. 16. Sudan Panthi: A WHO representative in Nepal, addressing health and sanitation issues. 17. Jennifer Piccin: From One Drop in Canada, focusing on water and sanitation projects. 18. Federico Properzi: Representing UN Water in Switzerland, contributing to global water initiatives. 19. Rochelle Rainey: From USAID in the USA, working on international development and health. 20. Pavani Ram: Another USAID representative in the USA, focusing on health and hygiene. 21. Anthony Rock: From Global Water 2020 in the USA, addressing water-related challenges. 22. Chandrakant Ruparelia: Representing Jhpiego in the USA, focusing on healthcare improvements. 23. Steve Sara: From Save the Children in the USA, contributing to child health and safety. 24. Manjeet Saluja: A WHO representative in India, addressing public health concerns. 25. Deepak Saxena: From the Indian Institute of Public Health, contributing to health research and education. 26. Oliver Schmoll: Based at the WHO European Centre for Environment and Health in Bonn, Germany, focusing on environmental health. 27. Theresa Shaver: From USAID in the USA, working on international health initiatives. 28. Enkhtsetseg Shinee: Also from the WHO European Centre for Environment and Health in Bonn, Germany, addressing health and sanitation. 29. Tom Slaymaker: Representing UNICEF in the USA, focusing on water and sanitation. 30. Elizabeth Tayler: A WHO representative in Switzerland, contributing to global health strategies. 31. Lavuuna Verstraete: From UNICEF in Zambia, addressing health and hygiene challenges. 32. Rob Quick: From the CDC in the USA, contributing to disease prevention and health promotion. 33. Willbald Zeck: Representing UNICEF in the USA, focusing on child health and development. Financial Support Acknowledgments: WHO and UNICEF express their gratitude to the following organizations for their financial contributions to WASH initiatives: Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) Netherlands Directorate-General for International Cooperation (DGIS) General Electric (GE) Foundation Global Environment Facility/United Nations Development Programme Conrad N. Hilton Foundation New Venture Fund Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) United Kingdom Department for International Development (DFID) United States Agency for International Development (USAID) For further information on the global status of WASH in healthcare facilities, refer to the companion document by the WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme for Water Supply, Sanitation, and Hygiene. The guiding principle remains: First, do no harm.
